stem:
$\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ reacts with $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ in the Haber process, as shown in reaction 1.

reaction 1 $$\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H = -x \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Table 2.1 shows the different conditions used to produce three equilibrium mixtures, **A**, **B** and **C**.

Table 2.1

|  | **A** | **B** | **C** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| initial molar ratio of $\text{N}_2 : \text{H}_2$ added | 1 : 3 | 1 : 3 | 1 : 3 |
| temperature/$^{\circ}\text{C}$ | 500 | 500 | 1000 |
| pressure/atm | 1000 | 1000 | 1000 |
| iron present in mixture | no | yes | no |
| percentage yield of $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$ at equilibrium | 58 | x | y |

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe and explain the change, if any, to the percentage yield of $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$ produced in **B** compared to **A**.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Describe and explain the change, if any, to the percentage yield of $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$ produced in **C** compared to **A**.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Describe and explain the change to the rate of the forward reaction that occurs to establish the equilibrium in **C** compared to **A**.

You do **not** need to refer to the Boltzmann distribution in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Write an expression for the equilibrium constant, $K_{\text{p}}$, for reaction 1. State the units.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Equilibrium mixture **D** is made when 1.0 mol of $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ and 3.0 mol of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ are added to a sealed container at $750^{\circ}\text{C}$ and 1000 atm and left to reach equilibrium. This mixture contains 1.16 mol of $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$.

Calculate the mole fraction of $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$ in **D**.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The mole fraction of $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ is 0.625 in a new equilibrium mixture, **E**.

Calculate the partial pressure of $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ in **E** when the total pressure is 1000 atm.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
When oxides of nitrogen escape into the atmosphere they may be involved in:

- formation of acid rain from sulfur dioxide
- formation of photochemical smog.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Identify the role of NO and $\text{NO}_2$ in the formation of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ from $\text{SO}_2$ in the atmosphere to produce acid rain.

Use relevant equations to support your answer.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Outline how NO and $\text{NO}_2$ may contribute to the formation of photochemical smog.
